newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL-Swedish Q2 GDP seen rising 2.1 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Swedish Q2 GDP seen rising 2.1 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Sweden's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was expected to rise 0.7 percent in the second quarter of 1997 compared with the first quarter, seasonally adjusted, and by 2.1 percent from a year ago, a Reuters poll found on Friday.
Forecasts varied between 0.2-1.5 percent for the quarter on quarter rise.
For the year, forecasts varied between 1.5-2.9 percent.
GDP in the second quarter of 1996 rose 0.3 percent, seasonally adjusted, while the year showed a rise of 0.5 percent.
In the first quarter of 1997, GDP fell 0.3 percent seasonally adjusted from the previous quarter and rose 1.6 percent from the same period a year earlier.
For the full year 1996 GDP rose by an average 1.1 percent.
For 1997 the economists expected GDP to increase by an average 2.3 percent. Forecasts ranged from 1.9 to 2.8 percent.
Statistics Sweden will release GDP figures for the second quarter on August 7 at 1100 GMT.

Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, I.D.E.A, JP Morgan, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, Penser, PaineWebber, Paribas, S-E-Banken, Union Bank of Switzerland, Unibank Markets.
